what_its_for: Cenegermin-bkbj is used to treat a serious eye condition called neurotrophic keratitis. This is a rare disease where the cornea (the clear front part of your eye) loses feeling and cannot heal properly on its own, leading to damage or sores on the eye surface. This medicine is a special protein (called a nerve growth factor) that helps your cornea heal and regrow healthy cells.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as eye drops. Before using, wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. Remove contact lenses before putting in the drops — wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Tilt your head back, gently pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket, and place one drop into the affected eye. Try not to touch the tip of the dropper to your eye, eyelid, or any other surface to avoid contamination. Blink gently after applying. If you use other eye drops or ointments, wait at least 15 minutes between each one. Always use cenegermin-bkbj last if using multiple eye products.
dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye(s) 6 times per day, spaced about 2 hours apart (for example: 7am, 9am, 11am, 1pm, 3pm, and 5pm). Treatment lasts for 8 weeks. Each single-use vial should only be used for one dose — throw away any leftover drops in the vial after each use. Do not save opened vials for later.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip that dose and take your next dose at the next scheduled time. Do not double up or use extra drops to make up for a missed one. Try to stay on your regular schedule as closely as possible.
storage: Keep unused vials in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze. Keep them in the original carton to protect from light. Once you remove the carton from the refrigerator for use, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 8 weeks. Always throw away any open vial after use — do not reuse. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear contact lenses during your 8-week treatment period without talking to your doctor first. Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface, including your eye, to prevent contamination. Do not use the drops if the solution appears cloudy or contains particles. Avoid rubbing your eyes after applying the drops. Do not drive or operate machinery if your vision is blurry right after applying the drops — wait until your vision clears.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: increased eye pain, redness, swelling, or discharge; sudden changes in your vision; signs of eye infection such as increased warmth, pus, or worsening redness; severe eye irritation or allergic reaction (itching, rash, swelling of face or throat, difficulty breathing). Call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse during your treatment.
when_it_works: Improvement in your eye may begin within the first few weeks of treatment, but it can take the full 8 weeks to see the most benefit. Everyone responds differently. Even if your eye starts feeling better, it is important to complete all 8 weeks of treatment as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not fully known — your doctor will help weigh the risks and benefits. Children: This medicine has been studied and can be used in children, including newborns, under the direction of a doctor. Older adults: No special dose adjustments are needed for older adults. Kidney or liver disease: No dose adjustments are expected, but always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions.
